title: The labelling queue in plain words: the question, the facts as sentences, the dataset, readable names first
request: The owner, labelling real-table disagreements: the questions and columns are not clear; make them simpler.
spec: dclab_rnd/ledger/labels.py (29.8 blind queue, 29.11 teaching order); dclab_core.ledger.blind_view.
plan: The dataset's name and its page for a real table.
An order with readable names first, labels taught (never counted).

decisions.decision: Readable-first labels are taught, never counted.
decisions.why: A sample chosen by its names is not fair; the promotion figures must come from the fair queue.

decisions.decision: The raw facts stay, folded under the sentences.
decisions.why: The sentences are a reading of the same bands; the bands remain the record.

change: dclab_rnd/ledger/labels.py (PLAIN, facts, readable, explain, the readable order), agentic/pages/ledger.py, web/src/views/admin.html, tests/test_label_queue.py

findings.defect: The labelling questions were hard to answer.
findings.scenario: Columns named oz58 or V10 with a target oz101, and a question in technical words.
findings.cause: The queue showed the raw state and the point's formal question.
findings.fix: Plain question, facts in words, the dataset and its link, readable names first.

measurements.name: the queue tests
measurements.result: label queue 10, active learning 6, web build 6, api contract 8
limits: the readable order scans every record: about 12 seconds on 42,000 decisions

outcome: A person can label real-table disagreements without decoding the state.
lessons: A label is only as good as the question a person can read.
risks: Readable-first labels teach but cannot show a student is better.
